activities.anchor: Grasping that ratio is not a party trick
activities.caption: sequence life on the calendar year
activities.name: ftCalendarOrder

config.prompt: Earth's history compressed to one calendar year — put the milestones in order:
items: All of recorded human history — the last half-minute before midnight on 31 December
config.why: The ratio is the subject's prerequisite: evolution needs billions of generations, plate tectonics centimetres per year across eons — the frame the whole subject hangs on.

activities.anchor: so sound they still open every geology course
activities.caption: which relative-dating principle applies?
activities.name: ftPrinciplesSort

config.prompt: Ordering without numbers — file each observation under its principle:

items.label: in an undisturbed stack, the lower layers are older
flat deposition, so tilted strata were deformed after deposition
you cannot break what is not there yet
a fault or intrusion must be younger than the rocks it cuts
a rock fragment inside another rock is older than its host

config.why: A handful of principles ordered every rock unit on Earth into one chronological column before anyone could put a number on it.

activities.caption: pair each concept with its landmark
activities.name: ftSmithMatch

config.prompt: The relative-dating toolkit — pair each piece with its landmark:

pairs.right: fossils appear in a definite, repeatable vertical order — valley after valley
the first geological map of England and Wales
surfaces where missing time is recorded — erosion or a pause
the same species, the same age — across a country and continents

config.why: Fossil content correlates rocks of the same age — the ordering system that named the chapters (Cambrian, Jurassic) a century before isotopes numbered them.

activities.anchor: one of science's great public-health victories hiding inside a dating paper
activities.caption: call the age of the Earth
activities.name: ftEarthAgeEst

config.prompt: Patterson's 1956 dating of meteorites settled the planet's age — call it.
config.why: 4.54 ± 0.05 billion years — meteorites are leftovers of solar-system formation, untouched, because Earth's own surface rocks recycle and are younger than the planet.
config.context: The oldest known terrestrial material is a U–Pb-dated zircon grain from Western Australia: 4.4 billion years.

activities.caption: true or false — the carbon-14 wristwatch
activities.name: ftC14Judge

statements.s: Carbon-14 can date a dinosaur directly.
statements.why: It reads organic material only to about 50,000 years — the dinosaur gets its date from the volcanic ash layers bracketing it (U–Pb).
Which is why the method runs out so fast — geology's wristwatch, not its calendar.

statements.s: The carbon-14 method dates volcanic rock.
statements.why: It dates organics; K–Ar is the volcanic-rocks clock.

statements.s: Willard Libby won the 1960 Nobel Prize for radiocarbon dating.

activities.anchor: a pollution catastrophe for the old biosphere that made ours possible
activities.caption: sequence the Precambrian into the Phanerozoic
activities.name: ftEonsOrder

config.prompt: The eons in order, with their landmarks:
items: Hadean — planetary formation; a Mars-sized collision splashes out the Moon
Archean — the first widely accepted traces of life: stromatolites ~3.5 billion years old
Proterozoic — the Great Oxidation Event, ~2.4 billion years ago
Phanerozoic — visible life: the Cambrian explosion opens the last 539 million years
config.why: The first 4 billion years are subdivided coarsely because fossils are sparse; the last 539 million are finely divided because fossils are abundant.

activities.anchor: rewrites the period's diversity every time a new quarry is worked
activities.caption: fill the blanks — what preservation demands
activities.name: ftPreserveCloze

config.text: Preservation is rare and biased: it needs %%0%% parts — shell, bone, teeth — plus rapid %%1%% and low %%2%%, which is why soft-bodied creatures are underrepresented and we have more fossils of clams than of caterpillars.
config.hint: Three conditions — one about anatomy, one about speed, one about the water's chemistry.

activities.anchor: regardless of their local numbers or thicknesses
activities.caption: correlate three quarries — walk the two-step
activities.name: ftQuarryBranch

config.root: Three quarries on opposite sides of a basin expose limestone beds with no visible way to line them up.

start.text: Quarry A's bed 3 holds Ammonites parkinsoni — a century of records spans it to a narrow Jurassic slice. Quarry B's bed 7 has the same species.

choices.label: Correlate the two beds as the same age
choices.feedback: The short-tenure species pins the age — correlation comes first, numbers second.

choices.label: Wait for radiometric dates on every bed
choices.feedback: U–Pb needs an ash bed to date — and there is none here yet; the fossil draws the line first.

c.text: Quarry C's bed 2 has the same ammonite, plus a distinctive foraminiferan.

choices.label: Correlate it too — same age as A and B
choices.feedback: Right — the shared short-tenure ammonite does the pinning; the extra foraminiferan refines the slice.

choices.label: Call it a different age — it has an extra fossil
choices.feedback: An added species does not move the age — the shared short-tenure one anchors it.

done.text: And if a thin volcanic ash sits just above the ammonite in quarry B, one U–Pb date on its zircons stamps all three beds at once — index fossil for the line, ash bed for the number.

wrongtool.text: Without an ash bed there is nothing to date isotopically — faunal succession is what correlates, and it built the old timescale before any isotope existed.

extra.text: Correlation keys on the species with wide range and short tenure — abundance is what makes it findable everywhere.

config.why: Faunal succession draws the lines, radiometric dating pins the pins — and each anchors the other's errors.
